I will plant the crops I know best and can manage steadily: winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same land. In Quzhou County, that rotation fits the climate, the water conditions, and the way I work. At my age, I do not want to gamble on a crop that needs more marketing skill or more hand labor. I want grain that I can sell easily, keep some for the household if needed, and manage with familiar timing. I will keep the land in the wheat-maize cycle, use improved seed, put most of my money into fertilizer and timely field work, and keep irrigation and spraying to the level needed to protect yield without wasting cash. For wheat I will focus on basal fertilizer, one or two topdressings, weed and disease control, and a few irrigations at key stages. After wheat harvest, I will seed maize quickly, keep the soil moisture, feed it enough nitrogen, and control weeds and insects on time. I will keep the plan simple, practical, and low-risk because that is what I trust most.
